result.title: TRIDENT and SHAKTI: A Framework and Benchmark for Hindi AI-Text Detection
result.summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly multilingual, distinguishing human-written from AI-generated text is essential for maintaining information integrity. However, research remains English-centric, with limited benchmarks for low-resource languages such as Hindi. To address this gap, we introduce SHAKTI, a large-scale Hindi benchmark covering four genres, eight LLM families, multiple prompting strategies, and adversarial transformations. We evaluate its quality through human annotation and analyze linguistic, grammatical, and sentiment-based differences between human- and AI-generated texts. Building on these findings, we propose TRIDENT, a round-trip translation-based detection framework with three variants: TRIDENT-S (static threshold), TRIDENT-D (dynamic threshold), and TRIDENT-C (logistic regression using multi-distance RTT features). TRIDENT leverages semantic consistency between original and round-trip translated texts to identify AI-generated content. Extensive experiments show that TRIDENT outperforms conventional and supervised baselines, with TRIDENT-S achieving the best overall performance. Further evaluations across seven languages, adversarial settings, and unseen LLMs demonstrate its multilingual applicability and robustness, while highlighting sensitivity to the translation model.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文构建了面向印地语的 AI 生成文本检测基准 SHAKTI，并提出基于往返翻译语义一致性的检测框架 TRIDENT，比较静态阈值、动态阈值与多距离特征回归三种变体。
AI.relevance_reason: 「往返变换后语义一致性」可作为评价指标的思路，可能启发对 LVR 中隐状态内容在改写或重渲染等可逆变换下是否保持一致的核查，但与视觉推理主线距离较远。
